source.title: Probing for Representation Manifolds in Superposition

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and applies a probe for continuous-concept representation manifolds, using additive superposition as a theoretical framework. It does not test whether individual neurons are polysemantic or test any of the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures linearly predictable time and space features in Llama 2-7b residual-stream representations and tests steering along a learned time manifold. These are related to representation geometry and superposition, but it does not measure individual-neuron responses to unrelated inputs, feature capacity pressure, or polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces a probe for continuous-concept manifolds in Llama 2-7b's residual stream and assumes additive superposition of concept representations (Definition 1) as a framework. It never examines individual neurons, polysemanticity rates, capacity pressure, architecture effects or measurement choices, so it tests none of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The author introduces the Manifold Probe for representation manifolds in superposition and finds interpretable linearly represented time and space features in Llama 2-7b. Steering along the time manifold influences release-year completions, which the author takes as evidence that the manifold is causally involved in model behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a supervised Manifold Probe for continuous representation manifolds and uses manifold-based residual-stream steering; it does not reproduce a neuron-polysemanticity method from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering efficacy varies with intervention layer, target year, and the work's release decade.

fits_no_version.finding: The Manifold Probe finds multiple linearly predictable features of release time and U.S. location in Llama 2-7b residual streams. Varimax-rotated features separate decades and many U.S. states; values are shown in figures only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuous concepts are represented on multi-dimensional manifolds in LM residual streams, encoding many linearly decodable features beyond the concept value.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding manifold-traced steering vectors shifts year completions toward targets. Efficacy peaks around layers 8 and 14 and falls to baseline from layer 20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned continuous-concept manifolds are causally used by the model, with layer-dependent steering efficacy.

record.problems: The study uses one model. Numeric feature-prediction and steering results are presented in figures rather than stated in the text. The paper notes that its framework may require tens of thousands of examples for good statistical performance in large foundation models. It does not measure neuron-level polysemanticity.

untested.parts: Vision-model neurons responding to unrelated inputs
Share of LM MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens, and its variation by layer
Superposition (more sparse features than neurons) as the cause of polysemanticity; additive superposition is assumed, not tested
Effects of architecture, activation function or regularization on polysemantic share
Whether polysemantic neurons are misread single features
Whether polysemanticity depends on activation range or scoring choices

record.verdict_notes: Uses 'superposition' in the additive-representation sense, not the neuron-packing sense. Single author, preprint, one model. No neuron-level analysis, so it has no bearing on the polysemantic-neuron claim.

versions.untested_parts: Vision models and individual neurons responding to unrelated image inputs.
The share of MLP neurons in transformer language models responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, including layer differences.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons and packing features together.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Comparisons of activation functions, architectures, or regularization for their effects on polysemantic-neuron share and performance.
Whether apparently mixed neuron responses share a coherent feature or job when examined with better tools.
Whether polysemanticity judgments depend on activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Fit Manifold Probe features to release dates and predict them linearly from residual-stream representations.

conditions.value: release time of songs, movies, and books
all layers; layer 16 is shown in Figures 1 and 3 reports results by layer

rows.measure: Test R² of learned features; comparison with ridge regression fitted directly to release dates.
rows.baseline: Direct release-date ridge regression; figure only
rows.value: Figure only. The text says the highest-ranked feature is close to the identity feature and tracks the direct-year result across layers.
rows.note: The text also says the probe finds additional linearly predictable features beyond the concept values themselves. This measures continuous-concept feature predictability, not individual-neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Residual-stream feature predictability for release dates. This is not a neuron-level polysemanticity measure. The 'observed' state is relative to the study's own goal, not to any claim version.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Fit Manifold Probe features to geographic coordinates and predict them linearly from residual-stream representations.

conditions.value: geographic coordinates of places in the U.S.A.
all layers; layer 16 is shown in Figure 2 and results by layer in Figure 3

rows.measure: Test R² of learned features; comparison with ridge regression fitted directly to latitude and longitude.
rows.baseline: Direct latitude and longitude ridge regressions; figure only
rows.value: Figure only. The text says the highest-ranked feature has a higher test R² than the latitude and longitude features, and that location representations consistently contain three considerably more predictable features than the rest.
rows.note: The probe's rotated space features localize on many U.S. states. These are feature-manifold findings, not measurements of individual-neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Residual-stream feature predictability for U.S. coordinates, unrelated to any version. The record says 'highest-ranked feature has higher R² than latitude and longitude'. The text attributes this to the 'time representations', apparently a typo for space.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Add a learned time-manifold steering vector to the last-token residual-stream activation.

conditions.value: 1,400 test-set works, stratified with 200 from each decade
layer sweep; the text identifies layers 8 and 14 as peaks for different release decades, with performance at baseline from layer 20 onward

rows.measure: Mean probability that a completion year is within two years of the target year.
rows.value: Figure only. The text reports that efficacy peaks at layers 8 and 14 depending on the work's release decade, falls sharply after layer 15, reaches baseline at layer 20 and beyond, and depends substantially on the target year.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations are shown in Figure 7; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe the interventions as having some success at steering completions toward target years. This is a causal steering result, not a test of neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: A steering efficacy result for the study's own manifold method. It does not measure polysemantic neurons, so the state relative to the claim cannot be determined.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
